scope: One machine, one pinned Julia environment, five fixed unbounded objectives, Strategy(0), warmed core MIGRAD only.
operation: Fresh counted callback and initial user-state/core solver construction; full core MIGRAD (C++ VariableMetricMinimizer::Minimize vs Julia migrad); owned parameter vector, error vector and full row-major covariance materialization; fval, EDM, NFcn, actual callback count, validity, covariance and termination flags. Five unbounded cases: internal parameters equal external parameters. Excludes immutable Gaussian input parsing/preparation, optional global correlation coefficients, JSON serialization. Julia BenchmarkTools uses gctrial=true,gcsample=false,overhead=0; C++ steady_clock surrounds one complete operation.
cpp_compiler:
Apple clang version 17.0.0 (clang-1700.0.13.5)
Target: arm64-apple-darwin24.6.0
Thread model: posix
InstalledDir: /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin

timing_protocol.summary: median of five paired median ratios; minimum and maximum of those five ratios

uncertainty: Report five paired median ratios and their observed range; descriptive interleaved variation, no population confidence interval or universal speed claim.
limitations: Single Apple M3 machine and Julia1.12.6 environment.
Thermal state, power state and unrelated background load were not controlled.
These are warmed core-MIGRAD operation timings; no loading/compilation or MnMigrad facade/global-correlation timing.
Each language retains its native allocation and object-reclamation costs.
No benchmarked numerical source was optimized or changed for this comparison.
Rosenbrock strict result parity failed; its ratios are not admitted.
